name: French Polynesia
summary: French civil law applies, so children have a protected share (the réserve) that a will cannot cut. A foreign resident cannot choose their national law, and the EU Succession Regulation does not apply. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force for France.
reserved_share: Children: 1/2 with one child, 2/3 with two, 3/4 with three or more (Code civil art 913); if no descendants, a surviving spouse 1/4 (art 914-1).
foreign_law_note: The EU Succession Regulation does not apply in French Polynesia (an overseas country and territory). Under French common-law conflict rules, land follows the law of its location and movables the last domicile, so a resident cannot select national law (not verified from a Polynesian source).
trust_note: The fiducie (Code civil arts 2011 ff.) is a statutory trust with narrow uses; its extension to French Polynesia was not verified. France has signed but not ratified the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations: only charitable forms known in France; local availability not verified.
open_questions: Which civil law rules apply locally and how the réserve applies to land under local land-tenure rules.
Whether fiducie and fondation law extend to French Polynesia.
